shadows.name: field-gap
shadows.purpose: Not a shadow: a zero-blur 3px halo in the field colour that cuts the ribbon where it passes behind the bow button on the magenta field. The system is otherwise flat.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: House ease-out for settles, hero text rise, ribbon lettering, bow-button swing.

motion.name: photo-reveal
motion.value: opacity 1.15s cubic-bezier(.22,.61,.36,1); transform scale(1.045)->none 1.8s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1); placeholder fades out after .9s
motion.purpose: Photo fades and settles over its pre-blurred placeholder.

motion.name: ribbon-entry
motion.purpose: On load, the ribbon leaves the needle's eye and winds round the hero arm (until the visitor scrolls).

motion.name: ribbon-unwind
motion.value: draw-length follows the deepest point reached (scroll + 86% viewport); chase 1 - exp(-3.2 dt), at least 900px/s; never rewinds
motion.purpose: The one authored moment: the ribbon unwinds along its length with the scroll.

motion.name: bow-tie
motion.value: 1500ms once the band reaches the knot: tails and loops draw, then the knot scales .4->1 with back-ease overshoot (1.70158); button swing 'etiqueta' 1.4s at 62%
motion.purpose: The bow ties over the last button.

motion.name: hero-rise
motion.purpose: Quiet entrance of the hero copy.

motion.name: state
motion.value: dotwork opacity .25s; band colour .2s; header ground .35s; banner word colour .5s

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce -> full ribbon and tied bow drawn static; photos and captions at rest; no smooth scroll

narrative.overview:
The whole system is one object taken from her logo: an S drawn as a ribbon wound round a vertical needle (Schleife is German for bow). On the page that ribbon is literal. It leaves the needle's eye in the first viewport, winds behind and in front of her work, flattens into a traditional tattoo banner behind every section word, and ties itself into a bow over the last booking button. Everything else holds still so the ribbon and her photographs carry the page.

The ground is velvet black, taken from the backdrop of her own photos, so the work appears to sit in the same space it was shot in. Her exact logo magenta is the only colour with a voice. Paper white appears only where her drawings live, and one section is drenched in magenta, where the ribbon turns white exactly as it does in the logo. States change technique, not tint: dotwork on hover, an inverted field on press, a dotted stencil line for focus. Type runs from billboard Fraktur down to footnote-sized tabular labels, and the practical copy stays in a plain grotesk.

The world refuses the dark-studio default: no grunge texture, no masonry Instagram grid, no neon accent, no clip-art iconography.
keyCharacteristics: One continuous SVG ribbon, generated from the layout, is the signature and the only decoration.
Flat colour only. Depth comes from the ribbon passing in front of and behind content, never from shadows.
Three grounds with fixed jobs: black for photographs, paper for drawings, magenta field for booking.
Square corners everywhere. The one non-rectangular silhouette is the swallowtail ribbon end.
One authored motion: the ribbon unwinding with the scroll and tying the bow. Reduced motion shows it whole and still.

rules.name: The One Magenta Rule
rules.body: Magenta is the brand colour at its exact value or it is absent. Shade comes from black hatching and highlight from white, never from a derived tint of the magenta.

rules.name: The Three Grounds Rule
rules.body: Black holds photographs, paper holds drawings, the magenta field holds booking. A new section takes the ground of what it shows. Paper does not become a card on black.

rules.name: The Banner Word Rule
rules.body: Fraktur only appears on a banner (section names, the phone menu) or as her name. It is never used for sentences, buttons or labels.

rules.name: The Ribbon-Sized Type Rule
rules.body: Banner words are sized from the ribbon width (spacing.ribbon), never on their own scale. Change the ribbon and the banners follow.

rules.name: The Plain Register Rule
rules.body: Anything practical (steps, captions, buttons, navigation) is set in Archivo. Facts such as dates and steps use tabular lining figures.

rules.name: The Field Gap Rule
rules.body: Where two white or magenta things overlap on the magenta field, they are separated by a gap of field colour, as in her monogram, never by an outline or a shadow. The knot carries a magenta stroke painted under its fill. The last button wears a zero-blur 3px magenta halo on all four sides (four drop-shadow offsets of 3px in the field colour), so the ribbon passing behind it reads as cut.

rules.name: The Ink Outline Rule
rules.body: A black ink outline (1.3px, round joins) on the ribbon appears only over paper, where flat magenta against white needs a drawn edge. It never appears on black or on the field.

rules.name: The Swallowtail Rule
rules.body: A shape that is not a rectangle is a piece of ribbon: swallowtail ends, never rounded pills.

dos: Do use the logo magenta at its exact value (colors.magenta) for the ribbon front, primary buttons and the booking field.
Do shade the ribbon's reverse with 45° hatching only: black on magenta, magenta on white.
Do separate overlapping shapes on the magenta field with a field-colour gap, as her monogram does.
Do size banner words from the ribbon width, so type and ribbon move together.
Do change state by technique: dotwork on hover, inversion on press, a 2px dotted line 5px off for focus.
Do give every photo a blurred placeholder in its exact box and reveal it with the fade-and-settle.
Do make reduced motion a finished state: the full ribbon and the tied bow, drawn and still.
Do keep every target at least 44px tall, and keep the first booking button inside the first phone screen from 320×640 up.
donts: Don't tint, lighten or gradient the magenta. Shading is hatching, never a derived tone.
Don't put Fraktur on sentences, buttons or labels. It belongs to banner words, the phone menu and her name.
Don't add soft or offset shadows, blur or rounded corners. The only halo is the zero-blur field-colour gap.
Don't draw the ink outline on the ribbon anywhere but over paper.
Don't use paper white as a card on black. Paper is a full section, for drawings.
Don't add grunge texture, a masonry grid, a neon accent or stock clip-art. Her own drawings, skull girl included, are the only illustrations.
Don't add a second authored animation. The ribbon unwinding and the bow tying are the moment; everything else is a quiet reveal.
